IN_FLIGHT.because: A committed SES recipient send is an immutable, irreversible occurrence: there is no desired-value replacement or external delete/restore operation for an email. Cancellation prevents future claims (the snapshot binding) but cannot undo an issued call. Its original attempt remains authoritative; profile C, generated evidence-confluence histories and the retained real two-connection late-result tests cover uncertainty, no blind resend and late settlement. This does not claim an escaped send can converge to cancellation.

debt.reason: orphaned_bulk_events() filters core_communityevent on email_sender_mode, email_notification_status, event_type and status, none of which lead an index, so the driving scan walks the table via core_communityevent_pkey with every predicate in Filter. The anti-join's inner Index Cond is the campaign lookup, not a narrowing of the events scanned. At a five-minute schedule the cost grows with every community event ever created. A partial index on the AWAITING/BULK/PAID predicate serves it, but that is a migration on a hot table and belongs in its own PR. strict=True so whoever adds it must delete this entry.

debt.reason: campaigns_due_for_unpark() has no index condition: no index leads on status or park_resume_after, so PostgreSQL reads the whole partial unique index one_active_campaign_per_event_kind (every non-terminal campaign) and filters PARKED and due. An index on park_resume_after WHERE status = 'PARKED' would serve it; that is a migration for its own PR. strict=True so whoever adds it must delete this entry.
